question: What layer does the Tungsten engine primarily optimize?
options: The logical query plan and rule-based rewrites
The cluster manager's resource negotiation
The metadata catalog and schema resolution
The physical execution: memory management and CPU efficiency
explanation: Tungsten focuses on the physical execution layer, improving memory and CPU efficiency through off-heap binary memory management, cache-aware computation, and whole-stage code generation. Catalyst handles the logical-plan side.

question: Why does Tungsten use off-heap memory and binary row formats?
options: To make debugging Java objects easier
To reduce JVM garbage collection overhead and object serialization costs
To bypass the need for executors entirely
To store all data permanently on local disk
explanation: By storing data as compact binary records in off-heap memory, Tungsten avoids the overhead of Java object headers and drastically reduces GC pressure, since the JVM garbage collector does not track off-heap regions the same way.

question: What is whole-stage code generation in Tungsten?
options: Generating a separate JVM per partition to isolate faults
Precompiling the entire application into machine code before submission
Fusing multiple operators in a stage into a single optimized JVM function at runtime
Generating shuffle files ahead of the actual shuffle
explanation: Whole-stage code generation collapses a chain of physical operators within a stage into one tight, generated Java function. This eliminates virtual function-call overhead and intermediate row materialization, letting the CPU run a fused loop over the data.

question: How does Tungsten's design aim to make Spark more CPU-efficient?
options: By keeping data cache-friendly and minimizing per-row virtual dispatch
By running all computation single-threaded to avoid contention
By moving computation from executors to the driver
By compressing all data with gzip before every operation
explanation: Tungsten uses cache-aware algorithms and compact binary layouts so data fits well in CPU caches, and whole-stage codegen removes the per-row virtual function-call overhead of the older iterator (Volcano) model, making the CPU the effective bottleneck rather than object overhead.

question: When you see 'WholeStageCodegen' nodes in a Spark physical plan, what does it indicate?
options: The query failed and fell back to interpreted execution
Operators in that stage were fused and compiled into generated bytecode for faster execution
The stage is being executed only on the driver
The data is being broadcast to all executors
explanation: A WholeStageCodegen node in the SQL/physical plan means Tungsten fused those operators and compiled them into a single generated function. Operators that don't support codegen appear outside these nodes and use the standard iterator model.
